data_status: STRICT MODE: this dataset contains only values that were compared with, or ingested directly from, retrieved sources: JPL (SSD, SBDB), NASA (NSSDC fact sheets and mission catalog, Small Spacecraft SoA report 2026, SLS page, Apollo 11 press kit, NTRS papers, ), ULA, ESA, NIST, and the Launch Library 2 aggregator. Records carry source_authority/confidence where the source is an aggregator or vendor-reported compilation. Recalled, estimated and fictional values (optimizer catalog, costs, engine/vehicle specs without a retrievable source, the user-supplied SpaceX table) are not included. Derived values are computed only from verified inputs and are labelled derived.

record.name: Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA)
record.description: The Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) will be used to produce a high-resolution (1 meter vertical resolution, 50 meter horizontal resolution) global topographic map and geodetic framework that enables precise targeting, safe landing, and surface mobility to carry out exploratory activities. It will also be used to detect surface ice inside permanently shadowed craters near the poles. LOLA consists of a side-pumped Nd:YAG laser which sends pulses through a diffractive optical element which breaks it into five beams. The beams form a cross pattern on the surface spanning about 50 meters. The range for each beam is determined by measuring the time of flight, the surface roughness is estimated from the pulse preading, and the surface reflectance is determined by the return signal strength. The reflectance will be particularly high if surface ice is present. LOLA will fire 28 shots per second and will make a total of over 4 billion measurements over the course of the mission. The time of flight is measured to 0.6 nanosecond precision which corresponds to 10 cm precision. After orbital uncertainties are included, the topography will be known to 50 meter horizontal accuracy and better than 1 meter vertical accuracy.
